title: A quiet place in my hometown
prompt: Describe a quiet place in your hometown that you enjoy visiting.
cuePoints: and explain why you enjoy spending time there

sentences.text: One place I particularly enjoy visiting is a small public garden near the river in my hometown.
It is only a short walk from my house, but it feels surprisingly removed from the traffic and noise of the main streets.
I first discovered it when a friend suggested taking a different route home after school.
Since then, I have made a habit of going there whenever I need to clear my head.
I usually visit in the early evening, when the air is cooler and the light reflects beautifully on the water.
Sometimes I bring a book, although I often end up simply watching people walk their dogs or chatting with a neighbour.
What makes the garden special is that it gives people a place to slow down without spending any money.
There are no impressive buildings or expensive attractions, just trees, comfortable benches and a sense of belonging.
For me, it is a reminder that a good quality of life often depends on ordinary spaces that bring a community together.
If I moved away, this would definitely be one of the places I would miss most.

title: My study routine
prompt: Do you prefer studying in the morning or in the evening?

sentences.text: I tend to study in the morning because I find it easier to concentrate before the day becomes busy.
For example, I usually spend half an hour reviewing my notes before checking my messages.
That small routine helps me feel more organised and gives me a clear idea of what I need to do next.
Having said that, I am quite flexible when I have a deadline, so I sometimes work in the evening as well.

title: Technology and communication
prompt: Has technology improved the way people communicate?

sentences.text: On balance, I think technology has made communication more accessible, especially for people who live far from their families.
A video call can help someone feel involved in an important occasion even when travelling is impossible.
However, convenience does not necessarily mean that every conversation becomes more meaningful.
When people constantly check notifications, they may pay less attention to the person sitting beside them.
I would therefore argue that the benefits depend largely on how deliberately we use these tools.
If we set aside distractions and choose the right form of communication for each situation, technology can support relationships rather than replace genuine human contact.
